requirement:
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.

A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`, so no implementation root is needed. The requirement has no Implements edges and the review roots are empty. Each clause states observable behavior only.

- "MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method with a body in the first-party Rust sources … including test functions, test helpers, and default trait methods." This sets which functions the check covers. A different parser or discovery mechanism would give the same results, so the choice of mechanism is discretionary.
- "Declarations without bodies MUST NOT create execution-coverage obligations." This describes outcomes only. Any implementation that creates no obligation for a bodiless declaration satisfies it.
- "Source discovery or parsing failures MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions." This is an observable failure condition. The text names no component that must own it. The parsing duty itself belongs to the cited `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, which is context only.
- "A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not measured rather than silently excluded." This is output behavior. It does not prescribe a type, field or signature.
- "Functions excluded by the selected build configuration require exception evidence under `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`." This delegates to the cited exceptions requirement. Its text is context, and any structural duties there belong to that requirement's own assessment.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or interface. Behavior-preserving alternatives exist for every clause. Behavioral evidence from tests is assessed under the behavioral criterion, not here.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`. I judged this from the supplied test source. I did not read the helpers `fixture`, `record`, `process` and `report`, or the implementation.

- **Functions with bodies are considered, including methods, test functions, helpers and default trait methods.**
  - `methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported` asserts a "zero execution" obligation for `impl[S]/fn[method]`, `mod[tests]/fn[case]` and `mod[tests]/fn[helper]`.
  - `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` asserts `#trait[T]/fn[body]: zero execution`.
  - `overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent` checks that nested functions are separate obligations. It also checks that a closure's execution does not cover its parent.
- **Declarations without bodies create no obligations.**
  - `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` asserts that `fn[declaration]` does not appear in the report. It also checks that a file with only a bodiless declaration, a macro call, or a derive has no function obligations.
  - `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` reports `code.rs: no executable obligations — pass` for a file containing only `struct S; trait T { fn declaration(); }`.
- **Discovery and parsing failures make the check fail.**
  - `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` writes malformed source (`fn malformed(`). It asserts `!result.passed` and that the report contains "cannot parse rust source".
  - `methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported` writes an invalid `.gitignore`. It asserts `!result.passed` and that the report contains "cannot discover reference sources".
- **A function whose measurement cannot be established is reported as not measured.** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` asserts both `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` and `#fn[missing]: not measured` when the file has no function measurements.
- **Functions excluded by the build configuration.** The `#[cfg(any())] fn excluded` case asserts `#fn[excluded]: not measured` and that the check does not pass. The exception-evidence rules belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions` and are not tested here.
- **First-party scope under `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`.** `post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor` shows that `src/vendor/first_party.rs` is included and fails the check. It also shows that the project-root `vendor/foreign.rs` is not reported.

I found no accepted behavior that violates the requirement and escapes these assertions.

text: :::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
